claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can initially exist in a high-temperature BCC state.
Homogenization at approximately 1200°C produces the stated high-temperature BCC initial state.
Phase stability is governed by competition between the thermodynamic driving force for compositional partitioning and kinetic limitations from atomic diffusion.
Al segregation is a particularly important component of the thermodynamic driving force for partitioning.
Exceeding a critical Al-diffusion threshold destabilizes the high-temperature BCC phase.
Destabilization of the BCC phase produces secondary phases such as B2 or FCC.
Insufficient diffusion kinetically preserves a metastable BCC structure.
Annealing at 750°C, 800°C, and 850°C with varied soak times can systematically vary the extent of diffusion.
Rapid transfer or quenching to the annealing temperature under an inert atmosphere minimizes oxidation.
Redistribution and enrichment of Al and Co facilitate nucleation of B2 or FCC within the BCC matrix.
Al segregation lowers the overall free energy of the system.
Atomic diffusion is required to realize the proposed thermodynamic benefit of segregation.
Sufficient atomic diffusion enables the nucleation barrier for secondary phases to be overcome.
At a fixed temperature, sufficiently long anneals will produce measurable secondary-phase fractions.
Secondary-phase fraction will increase with annealing time and correlate with diffusion-controlled compositional partitioning.
Short anneals at each temperature will retain the metastable BCC phase because diffusion is limited.
Transformation is bounded by a critical temperature–time combination that permits sufficient Al partitioning.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that the atomic diffusion rate must exceed a critical threshold, whereas the controlled comparison mainly varies soak time at fixed temperature. Longer time changes diffusion distance and partitioning extent but does not itself increase the diffusion coefficient; the proposed rate threshold is therefore not operationally aligned with the experiment.

The hypothesis invokes a critical diffusion threshold, but neither the threshold nor a method for determining that it has been exceeded is specified. Consequently, the phrase 'durations predicted to allow sufficient diffusion' can be adjusted after observing the result, weakening the stated falsification rule.
